chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: "Grooving High" and "How High the Moon"; Benny Harris and Garner
summary: Budd demonstrates how 'Grooving High' was built on 'How High the Moon' and 'Whispering', and mentions Erroll Garner and 'Misty'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right, I can tell you about-- what is it, 'Grooving High'?
Start that again and I'll sing the melody.
See. Now 'Grooving High' was nothing but 'How High the Moon', see. Was nothing but How High the Moon, see. (Singing of notes).
I went off a little key because I'm a worst singer.
Okay, but any way, now that tune came about because when we would play 'How High the Moon', that was Benny Harris' solo, the trumpet player.
Bobby Hackett and I the other night tried to remember Benny Harris' name and it came up two days later.

See, that was Benny Harris' solo, and if I'm not really mistaken so was Whispering Benny Harris' solo. And, you know -- but as I told you, cats never copyrighted anything in those days so you wind up with somebody else with your song and gone. You know what I mean?
That's right. So there was a lot of thievery going on that way also, with different tunes.
Those are two very good tunes.
Oh, well. Take Erroll Garner, which is a great piano player, you know.
Now, I'm trying to think of the song that -- Misty is written off of also. (Singing of notes).
Well, it's a song like that and we will remember it and get back to it because I know the song. But this is what guys were doing.
